{"self_assessment": "Impact: I drew the fish sketch on the scratch pad that the table built from. It gave the team one clear, big, side-on outline with a top line, a bottom line and a forked tail, so everyone was working from the same picture. I then laid the tail section myself, about 44 dominoes across two strokes that branch off the body. The tail is the feature that makes the outline read as a fish. My final inspection confirmed that all 143 standing dominoes were connected to the start, so the full outline was set to fall.

Execution: I fetched a load of dominoes for my own tray early, so I could lay the tail without waiting on supplies. I worked quietly and steadily on my section, then spent my remaining time inspecting the tail joins closely instead of adding more dominoes. Because of those checks I could say with confidence that the run was connected, and I told the table so before the push.

Collaboration: I split the bottom line with Tom at the deepest point of the belly, so we didn't work on top of each other. I also shared what I found about the lower fork with Leo and Tom. Once I confirmed everything was connected, I suggested everyone keep hands off, to avoid a bump right before the push. That kept the table calm and coordinated for the last few minutes.

Leadership: I took the sketch early and proposed a clear division of the lines, which gave the table a plan to build from. I claimed the tail and kept my work focused on it. When the picture was complete, I made the call to stop touching it and protect what we had built.", "my_share_percent": 30}
